name: synthesis-scenario-add-coupon-checkout
query: i need to repro a registered shopper adding a promo coupon to their basket and checking out -- on a sandbox. which SCAPI calls do i need in what order, and which scopes must the SLAS client have
hypothesis: Multi-call SCAPI plan must surface addCouponToBasket as the named coupon operation (verified in spec at shopper-baskets/addCouponToBasket.json: POST /organizations/{organizationId}/baskets/{basketId}/coupons, scopes [sfcc.shopper-baskets-orders.rw, sfcc.shopper-standard]), thread basketId from createBasket through to checkout, and cite both shopper-baskets and shopper-orders public reference URLs. The combined-scope assertion uses an alternation (sfcc.shopper-baskets-orders.rw | sfcc.shopper-(baskets|orders)) so that whether the model surfaces the rolled-up RW scope or the per-reference fallbacks both render as a pass. Tool-path assertions deliberately omitted (see iteration-synthesis-assertion-relaxation in dsc-endpoint-help).

assertions.because: the named SCAPI operation for adding a coupon must appear in the plan (verified real op in shopper-baskets spec)
must cite the public shopper-baskets reference URL
must cite the public shopper-orders reference URL -- proves the multi-reference plan walks both
scope union must surface either the rolled-up baskets-orders.rw scope or the per-reference fallbacks (both are valid per the spec's accepted-scope list on addCouponToBasket and createOrder)

SLAS leg 1 must be explicitly named as the authorizeCustomer operation -- per iteration-slas-mandatory-auth-expansion, auth is the universal precondition for every SCAPI call and the plan must include both SLAS legs as expanded steps (not just name the SLAS reference generically). Partial expansion that mentions the reference but doesn't name authorizeCustomer is no longer a pass -- the user can't make the call without knowing which operation to invoke.

SLAS leg 2 must be explicitly named as the getAccessToken operation -- both legs are required to actually obtain the bearer token, and the plan must show them as separate expanded steps. Pairs with the authorizeCustomer assertion above; this tightening makes the assertion intent (full SLAS expansion) sharper than the prior reference-OR-leg regex.

must cite the SLAS reference's public DSC URL. The reference's URL slug on developer.salesforce.com is `auth` (page title is 'Shopper Login (SLAS)' but the URL is /references/auth, not /references/shopper-login -- /references/shopper-login 404s). The negative lookahead `(?![a-zA-Z0-9_-])` enforces a slug boundary, so /references/auth and /references/auth?meta=authorizeCustomer pass while /references/auth-admin, /references/authentication, and /guide/authorization-... do not.

must NOT use the shrug phrasings flagged in iteration-todo-slas-cross-reference-prose.md. SLAS is a DSC reference; calling a SLAS step 'external' or 'not part of' the reference set misrepresents the skill's universe to the user.
citation-leak guard -- local cache paths must never appear in customer-facing answers

name: synthesis-scenario-ocapi-submit-basket
query: target op is OCAPI shop-orders `Submit basket` (POST /orders). what are the prerequisites -- which calls have to happen first and where does the basket_id come from? is the basket -> order chain the same as SCAPI?
hypothesis: OCAPI-targeted scenario must produce an OCAPI plan citing OCAPI shop reference URLs (anchored on `ocapi` so SCAPI's shopper-orders URL doesn't false-pass) using OCAPI path notation (`/dw/shop/v<version>/...`), and must NOT propose migrating to SCAPI -- the operator memory documents that customers migrate OFF OCAPI to SCAPI, never the reverse, and a scenario asking about an OCAPI target should answer the OCAPI question, not redirect. This fixture guards against the most likely failure mode: the model treats OCAPI as legacy and answers in SCAPI terms anyway.

assertions.because: must cite the public OCAPI shop reference URL (anchored on `ocapi` so SCAPI's shopper-orders or shopper-baskets reference -- which contains `shop` as a substring -- cannot false-pass this assertion)
must use OCAPI path notation -- proves the answer is an OCAPI plan and not silently translated into SCAPI's `/checkout/...` paths
must not propose OCAPI->SCAPI migration -- user explicitly asked about OCAPI; redirecting to SCAPI dodges the question
citation-leak guard -- local cache paths must never appear in customer-facing answers

name: synthesis-scenario-createorder-basketid-threading
query: target op is `shopper-orders.createOrder`. what are the prerequisites -- which calls have to happen first and where does the basketId come from?
hypothesis: Cascade-order regression guard for the existing worked example at docs/examples/scenario-createorder-prereqs/. Plan must explicitly surface that `basketId` is produced by `createBasket` and threaded into `createOrder`'s body; any answer that doesn't name both operations together fails the cascade-order assertion. The two URL assertions cite specific operation slugs (?meta=createBasket / ?meta=createOrder) so a generic reference-root URL doesn't false-pass. Tool-path assertions deliberately omitted (see iteration-synthesis-assertion-relaxation in dsc-endpoint-help).

assertions.because: basketId must be linked to createBasket explicitly (within ~400 chars of each other) -- proves the cascade-order analysis identified the producer relationship, not just listed operations side by side
must cite the public shopper-baskets reference URL with the createBasket operation slug -- proves the citation is operation-specific, not just a reference-root link
must cite the public shopper-orders reference URL with the createOrder operation slug -- proves the citation is operation-specific, not just a reference-root link

SLAS leg 1 must be explicitly named -- per iteration-slas-mandatory-auth-expansion, the createOrder-prereqs plan must show both SLAS legs as numbered steps. Same regression guard as on the add-coupon-checkout fixture; the worked example we re-capture from this fixture must show full SLAS expansion.

SLAS leg 2 must be explicitly named -- both legs required for the token exchange. Pairs with authorizeCustomer above; tightens what was previously a reference-OR-one-leg regex into a strict both-legs requirement.

must cite the SLAS reference's public DSC URL slug `auth` -- the operations must be backed by their reference's public URL. The reference is published at /references/auth on developer.salesforce.com (page title 'Shopper Login (SLAS)'); /references/shopper-login 404s, so a citation that uses that slug isn't actually shareable.
must NOT use the shrug phrasings flagged in iteration-todo-slas-cross-reference-prose.md
citation-leak guard -- local cache paths must never appear in customer-facing answers
